slides.heading: Vacuum Forming a Plastic Shell
bullets: How vacuum forming shapes a plastic shell: a clamped thermoplastic sheet is heated until pliable, then outside air pressure pushes it onto the mould
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one plastic sheet through the whole vacuum-forming cycle, from flat and rigid to a finished shell that keeps the shape of the mould.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Describe the vacuum-forming cycle in order: clamp, heat, form, cool and release
Explain why outside air pressure, not the vacuum, pushes the soft sheet onto the mould
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to order every stage of the cycle and explain what really does the pushing at the forming stage.

slides.heading: A flat sheet becomes a shell - what pushes it?
bullets: The sheet starts flat and rigid, clamped in a frame above the mould
So what force presses the soft sheet down onto every surface of the mould?
slides.notes: Ask the class: the machine is called a vacuum former, so does the vacuum pull the plastic down? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the vacuum only removes air.

slides.heading: Pressure pushes, the vacuum only removes air
bullets: A vacuum cannot pull - it only removes air from beneath the sheet
Outside air pressure, about 100,000 pascals on every square metre, is then unopposed
That unopposed pressure pushes the pliable sheet onto every surface of the mould
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: removing air leaves nothing pushing back, so the ordinary pressure of the air outside does all the forming work.

slides.heading: Setup: sheet clamped above the mould
bullets: A flat thermoplastic sheet is clamped in a frame above a mould on the machine bed, with a heater panel overhead
The mould rises toward the sheet to start the cycle
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the frame, the heater and the mould: name each part before anything is heated.

slides.heading: Heating: the sheet softens and sags
bullets: The heater warms the clamped sheet until the plastic becomes pliable
The softened sheet sags under its own weight, ready to be formed
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and watch the sheet sag: it is pliable now, but nothing has formed it yet.

slides.heading: Vacuum forming: air pressure pushes the sheet onto the mould
bullets: The mould rises into the soft sheet and the pump removes the air trapped beneath it
Outside air pressure, now unopposed, pushes the sheet down onto every surface of the mould
slides.notes: Play scene 3 slowly: the pump only removes air - watch the outside air pressure push the sheet onto the mould.

slides.heading: Cooling and release: the rigid shell lifts off
bullets: The formed sheet cools on the mould and sets rigid
The shell is lifted off and the excess edge is trimmed away, leaving a finished shell that keeps the mould shape
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and follow the cooling shell: once rigid it keeps the mould shape, so it can be lifted off and trimmed.

slides.heading: Worked example: tracing one cycle
bullets: Clamp the flat sheet, heat it until it sags pliable, raise the mould, remove the air beneath, and let outside pressure form it
Cool it rigid on the mould, lift the shell off, and trim the excess edge
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, clamp and heat. Step 2, the mould rises into the pliable sheet. Step 3, air is removed and outside pressure forms the sheet. Step 4, cool, release and trim.

slides.heading: Your turn: order the cycle
bullets: In pairs: put clamp, heat, form, cool and trim in order, and say what the vacuum actually does at the forming stage
Then swap and check: did your partner say the vacuum removes air and pressure pushes, instead of the vacuum pulling?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for pressure-pushes reasoning, then take two pairs answers: the vacuum removes the trapped air, and unopposed outside air pressure pushes the sheet onto the mould.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says the vacuum pulls the soft sheet down onto the mould
Name what the vacuum removes and what outside air pressure pushes to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers separate removing air from pushing - the vacuum does the first, the atmosphere does the second.
